dedupe_keys.name: national audit office update on the new hospital programme england january 2026

description: This National Audit Office report checks whether England's New Hospital Programme can now be delivered after the government reset it in January 2025. The programme began in 2020 with a promise of 40 new hospitals by 2030, which the NAO had judged unachievable in 2023. The update finds 46 schemes in total, five already open and 41 funded to be built in four waves over about twenty years: 19 new hospitals, 19 new buildings or wings, two major refurbishments and one still undecided. The seven hospitals built from crumbling RAAC concrete come first, with replacements due by 2032-33, while the last hospitals may not open until around 2045-46. The estimated total cost is about 60 billion pounds, and keeping old buildings running meanwhile costs trusts an extra 100 to 140 million pounds a year. The standard Hospital 2.0 design assumes 92 percent bed occupancy. The report summary is free to download as a PDF from the NAO website. Coverage is the NHS hospital building programme in England. Caveats: the NAO did not assess individual schemes or the wider NHS estate; benefit figures are DHSC's own estimates. Simulation uses: timelines, costs and capacity assumptions for long-range hospital capacity and estate risk scenarios. Related records: the scheme-level data tables are catalogued as data-dhsc-new-hospital-programme-annual-data.

name: National Audit Office: Update on the New Hospital Programme (England, January 2026)
organisations: Department of Health and Social Care
outcomes: 46 schemes in total (41 funded in January 2025 plus 5 already complete); estimated total cost about £60 billion from 2021-22; £9.6 billion confirmed for 2025-26 to 2029-30 and about £3 billion a year from 2030-31; final hospitals expected to open around 2045-46 and RAAC replacements complete by 2032-33; £100 to £140 million a year extra maintenance for buildings awaiting replacement; 39% vacancy rate in the NHP team (November 2025); Hospital 2.0 design assumes 92% bed occupancy and about 6% more overnight beds across 28 schemes; DHSC claims £3.10 return per £1 for a central programme against £2.70 for a trust-led approach.
provider: National Audit Office (UK), report HC 1594, session 2024 to 2026
resources_used: Earlier NAO report Progress with the New Hospital Programme (HC 1662, July 2023)
